versions.version: HpdfDocument.Pages follows the page tree (viewer) order; saving checks that every GSave has a GRestore; document dates honor DateTimeKind.Utc (new DateTimeOffset overloads); page labels always have an entry for the first page; SetXYZ, extended graphics state and page label values are validated as in the C library; generated font and image resource names start with "Haru". Fonts: text with non-ASCII characters is measured with the right glyph widths (standard 14 fonts by Unicode as in the C library, TrueType and Type1 fonts by their code page); Type1 fonts map all glyph names of the Adobe glyph list, so Central European and other non-Latin-1 glyphs are drawn and get their widths; the non-breaking space, the soft hyphen and other characters that share a glyph (Greek mu, Omega, Delta) are drawn and measured with that glyph; standard fonts draw the right glyphs with CP1251, CP1253, KOI8-R, ISO8859-14 and other encodings (the names of /Differences were shifted after a character without a glyph name) and have the Romanian T with comma below (ISO8859-16); TrueType text is measured with the widths written to /Widths; text shown with an embedded CID font (HpdfCIDFont) can be copied and searched with every code page, also CP932, CP936, CP949 and CP950 (the ToUnicode map is written from the glyphs shown when the document is saved; a glyph shared by two characters maps to the one that was shown), is measured with the glyphs it is drawn with whatever the code page, and the font's /W array holds only the glyphs in use; characters above U+FFFF (surrogate pairs, e.g. CJK Extension B) are drawn, measured, kept together when text is wrapped, and copied as one character when the font has them (cmap format 12; new overload HpdfCIDFont.GetGlyphId(Rune)). Predefined (not embedded) CJK fonts (HpdfCIDFontType0): character codes are mapped to CIDs with the CMap tables of the C library, so half-width and proportional characters are measured with their real widths; the /W array no longer gives CIDs 1-127 an invented width of 500 (some characters had two widths, and viewers spaced Latin text of the proportional fonts unevenly); MingLiU has the half-width Latin CIDs of its own character collection; the stub ToUnicode map is gone (a predefined CMap needs none); the encoder argument of HpdfCIDFontType0.Create may be omitted (new CIDEncoder.Create, GetCID and ReadCID). Predefined CJK fonts can be used with all the horizontal CMaps of the C library: GB-EUC-H, 90msp-RKSJ-H (the CMap of the proportional fonts MS-PGothic and MS-PMincho), KSCms-UHC-HW-H and KSC-EUC-H are new; a CMap name is found in any letter case; the font takes its code page from the CMap (new overload HpdfCIDFontType0.Create without the code page, which is no longer used). Vertical writing: a predefined CJK font created with a vertical CMap (GBK-EUC-V, GB-EUC-V, ETen-B5-V, 90ms-RKSJ-V, EUC-V, KSCms-UHC-HW-V, KSC-EUC-V) shows text from top to bottom with the vertical forms of brackets and punctuation; MeasureText gives the height of the text; new property WritingMode of HpdfFont, CIDEncoder and IHpdfFontImplementation; TextRect with a vertical font prints columns from the right edge of the rectangle to the left, one text leading apart, and aligns or justifies the text along the column; an embedded CID font can be loaded for vertical writing too (new overload HpdfCIDFont.LoadFromTrueTypeFile with HpdfWritingMode: Identity-V, with the vertical glyph forms of the font's GSUB 'vert' feature; each glyph advances by the height the font's vmtx table gives it and hangs from its own vertical origin (/W2); the text stays copyable). Line breaks in Chinese and Japanese text: TextRect and MeasureText with word wrapping break between characters where the typesetting rules allow - a line does not begin with a closing bracket, a full stop or comma, a small kana or the prolonged sound mark and does not end with an opening bracket (the character before moves to the next line); a Latin or Korean word next to such text is no longer cut where the line ends. Embedded TrueType and CID fonts are stored as subsets with the outlines of the glyphs in use (a TrueType font: the glyphs of its code page; a CID font: the glyphs shown), so a document with CJK text no longer carries the whole 5-10 MB font file; the font name in the PDF gets a subset tag; the new property EmbedSubset of HpdfTrueTypeFont and HpdfCIDFont switches back to the whole font file. Font collections (.ttc): a font of a TrueType collection is loaded by its index, from a file or a stream (new methods HpdfTrueTypeFont.LoadFromCollection, HpdfCIDFont.LoadFromTrueTypeCollection, FontDataPool.GetOrLoadTrueTypeCollection and property ParsedTrueTypeData.FontIndex, as HPDF_LoadTTFontFromFile2 of the C library) and embedded as a font of its own, never as the collection; a collection given to LoadFromFile or LoadFromTrueTypeFile throws InvalidTtcFile. OpenType fonts with CFF outlines (.otf, .otc) are embedded as CFF programs (FontFile3): a simple font (HpdfTrueTypeFont) becomes a Type1 font with a Type1C program, a CID font (HpdfCIDFont) a CIDFontType0 font with a CIDFontType0C program; subsets hold the glyphs in use without subroutines (about 250 bytes per glyph: tens of KB for a page of CJK text from a 16 MB font); vertical writing takes the origins of the VORG table (they were embedded as the whole OpenType file in FontFile2, which viewers reject or show wrong). Breaking: a CJK .otf font (CID-keyed CFF) loaded as HpdfTrueTypeFont throws UnsupportedFontType (use HpdfCIDFont); a font with neither TrueType nor CFF outlines cannot be embedded (TtfMissingTable). FontDataPool: the same font file can be loaded with several code pages (the second load returned the data of the first one); new overloads LoadFromSharedData(..., codePage) of HpdfTrueTypeFont and HpdfType1Font. Fonts by name: RegisterFont and GetFont understand the same encoding names (a font registered as "ISO8859-2" was not found by GetFont), in any letter case, including MacRomanEncoding, UTF-8 and the CJK CMap names; GetFont with the font name alone returns a registered font whatever its code page is; a font is registered under its encoding, not only its code page, so one font can be registered with encodings that share a code page (90ms-RKSJ-H, 90msp-RKSJ-H and 90ms-RKSJ-V; an embedded CID font for horizontal and for vertical writing, found by "Identity-H" / "UTF-8" and "Identity-V") - the later registration replaced the earlier. A font file without a PostScript name is named in the same way by every font kind (family and subfamily; FontDataPool no longer invents a random name). A simple TrueType font can be made from a font file that has only the cmap subtable for all of Unicode (format 12); FontDataPool parses a font file once for all the fonts created from it. The font descriptor of TrueType and CID fonts gives the font bounding box, ascent, descent and cap height in 1000-unit glyph space as a PDF requires (they were written in font units, twice too large for a font with 2048 units per em), the cap height is the height of the letter H, and the x-height is written (/XHeight). File structure: the entries of the cross-reference table are exactly 20 bytes long as the PDF format requires (they had one extra space, so strict readers such as MuPDF had to repair every file). Breaking: HpdfFont.GetCharWidth of a TrueType font returns 1000-unit glyph space as for the other fonts (was font units); a font whose embedding permissions (fsType) forbid embedding throws TtfCannotEmbeddingFont when it is loaded for embedding (a font that only forbids subsetting is embedded whole); HpdfCIDFontType0.Create without an encoder throws InvalidEncodingName for a CMap name the library has no encoder for; the default code page of FontDataPool.GetOrLoadTrueType is 1252 as everywhere else (was 437); GetFont and RegisterFont throw InvalidEncodingName for an unknown encoding name (it silently became WinAnsiEncoding); a standard font asked for with an encoding it does not have (GetFont("Helvetica", "UTF-8"), a CJK encoding, a code page such as 437) throws InvalidEncoderType instead of being written with WinAnsiEncoding; the enum Haru.Font.CID.CIDWritingMode, which no member used, is removed (Haru.Types.HpdfWritingMode is the writing mode); HpdfFont.GetXHeight of a TrueType or CID font returns the height of the letter x (it returned the typographic ascender), 0 if the font does not tell it. Annotations: markup annotations with appearance streams drawn when the document is saved - square, circle, line (line endings, captions, leader lines), polygon, polyline, ink, highlight, underline, squiggly, strike-out, caret, free text (callouts, cloudy borders), stamp and redaction - with pop-up windows, flags (HpdfAnnotation.Flags), replies and groups (/IRT), rich text (/RC), subjects and creation dates (new types HpdfMarkupAnnotation and its subclasses, HpdfPopupAnnotation, the HpdfPage.Create...Annotation methods and HpdfPage.Annotations). Document attachments (HpdfDocument.AttachFile, AttachedFiles, HpdfEmbeddedFile) and file attachment annotations. 3D: U3D and PRC models (HpdfDocument.Load3DModel, namespace Haru.ThreeD) shown by 3D annotations with views, cameras, lighting, nodes and an /OnInstantiate script, 3D measurements (comment notes, perpendicular measurements) and projection annotations; PRC models and measurements declare Adobe ExtensionLevel 3. Named destinations (HpdfDocument.CreateNamedDestination, HpdfNamedDestination: links and outline items go to a name, also before its page exists, and a URL opens the document at it with #nameddest=), document JavaScript (HpdfDocument.AddJavaScript) and links that run JavaScript (HpdfPage.CreateJavaScriptLinkAnnotation). Annotations, attachments and JavaScript raise the PDF version they need; saving a PDF/A-1 document fails for the annotation types PDF/A-1 does not allow, for embedded files and for JavaScript. A JavaScript program can run when the document is opened (HpdfDocument.SetOpenJavaScript, the open action). Images: new property HpdfImage.Interpolate (/Interpolate; not allowed in PDF/A-1).

System.Text.Encoding.CodePages dependency removed. Image transparency fixes (PNG alpha/color detection), validated color masks, reusable stencil masks, new HpdfImage.SetSoftMask. PDF version is raised automatically for transparency (1.4). Color masks work on gray images; a PNG is read from the current stream position. AcroForms: checkboxes, radio buttons and signature fields draw their own frame (colors from SetAppearanceCharacteristics), the appearance state always follows the field value, /SigFlags is set for signature fields; text and choice fields get appearance streams showing their values and the form gets default resources (/DR). New: HpdfPageText.TextRect, HpdfPage.Rotate, HpdfCatalog.ViewerPreferences and SetOpenAction, EoFillStroke/ClosePathEoFillStroke, SetFlat. Fixed: text measurement treated Unicode characters such as U+010A as line breaks; the text line position ignored the text matrix scale; a document could not be saved twice; non-ASCII text (field names, values and options, outline titles, document information) was written as UTF-8 and is now a PDF text string (UTF-16BE); with RC4 encryption only the first string of an object (e.g. of the document information) could be decrypted; non-ASCII link URIs are percent-encoded; Arc continues a path that is being built with a line (pie slices); outline /Count of closed nested items; TextRect honors horizontal scaling; setters such as SetBorderStyle, SetRgbColor, SetSlideShow, SetDestination can be called again; the compression mode applies to pages added before it was set; image masks and page labels raise the PDF version to 1.3; JPEG images are read from the current stream position. Validation as in the C library: GSave/GRestore nesting, invalid line cap/join/rendering mode, all-zero dash patterns, text without a font, equal arc angles, unsupported encryption modes, raw image bit depths, duplicate page resource names, widget colors, radio option names, choice values. Breaking: IElementAppearance has new members Caption and DrawFrame; IDrawable has the new member PathInProgress; Haru.Forms.HpdfTextAlignment is renamed to HpdfFieldAlignment (Haru.Types.HpdfTextAlignment is used by TextRect); HpdfString(string) writes a PDF text string instead of UTF-8; ShowText and related methods throw PageFontNotFound without a font; HpdfAcroForm has no public constructor (use GetOrCreateAcroForm); the duplicate extension method HpdfDocumentExtensions.LoadPngImageFromFile is removed; radio button groups accept only option widgets; HpdfSignature.SetValue/SetDefaultValue throw; SetEncryption requires an owner password that is not empty and differs from the user password (as in the C library) and accepts only Latin-1 passwords; the HpdfLinkAnnotation and HpdfTextAnnotation constructors are internal (use HpdfPage.CreateLinkAnnotation / CreateTextAnnotation, new overload with HpdfDestination); outline and link destinations need a view. Also: PDF/A sets the Print flag on annotations; PNG images load from forward-only streams.
Feature: Identity-H Unicode support in HpdfCIDFont. The skill for nuget-skills added.
Fully C# version of Haru PDF library.
